summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 17.3 to Angular 18.2 with `ng update @angular/core@18 @angular/cli@18`, whose core migration replaced the deprecated `HttpClientModule` import with `provideHttpClient(withInterceptorsFromDi())` in app.module.ts. @ngrx/* had to follow to 18.1.1 because the 17.2 line declares `@angular/core: ^17.0.0` as a peer, so a clean install would not resolve; the ngrx v18 migration rewrote the removed `TypedAction` type to `Action` but emitted a duplicate import that had to be fixed by hand. Install, build and the SSR build pass from a clean node_modules; tests still fail exactly as at baseline for the same pre-existing reason.
changes: ng update @angular/core@18 @angular/cli@18 bumped all @angular/* packages to 18.2.14 and @angular/cli / @angular-devkit/build-angular to 18.2.21.

The core v18 `HttpClientModule` migration removed `HttpClientModule` from the AppModule imports and added `provideHttpClient(withInterceptorsFromDi())` to providers. `withInterceptorsFromDi()` keeps the old DI-based HTTP_INTERCEPTORS behaviour, so this is behaviour-preserving.

Reformatted the @NgModule decorator in src/app/app.module.ts back to the file's original layout: the migration collapsed it into one-key-per-line-less form with 4-space indentation. Only whitespace, no semantic difference.

Bumped all five @ngrx/* packages from 17.2.0 to 18.1.1 via `ng update @ngrx/store@18 ...`. Required, not cosmetic: @ngrx 17's peer dependency on `@angular/core: ^17.0.0` makes a clean `npm install` unresolvable against Angular 18.

The ngrx v18 migration replaced `TypedAction` (removed in v18) with `Action` in src/app/state/reducers/employee.reducer.ts, but left two conflicting `Action` imports (one from '@ngrx/store', one from the old deep path '@ngrx/store/src/models'), which is a duplicate-identifier error. Dropped the deep-path import by hand; `reducer()` now takes the public `Action` type.

The ngrx migration also added `@ngrx/operators` to package.json for the `concatLatestFrom` move. This app never imports `concatLatestFrom` (nothing in src/ references @ngrx/operators), so the dependency was removed again via `npm uninstall` rather than left as an unused package.

No other Angular 18 breaking change applies: the app does not use `afterRender` phases, `bootstrapApplication`/`main.server.ts`, or invalid two-way bindings, and all three of those core migrations reported no changes.

rxjs stays at ^6.6.7: Angular 18.2's peer range is still `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0`, and @ngrx 18 accepts `^6.5.3 || ^7.5.0`, so rxjs 7 is still not forced by this hop. (The previous hop's report expected v18 to require it; it does not.)
zone.js stays at ~0.14.10 and TypeScript at 5.4.5, both inside Angular 18.2's peer ranges, so neither needed to move.

Declined the optional `use-application-builder` migration (esbuild/`application` builder). Angular 18 still supports the webpack `browser` builder this project uses, and switching builders would change the SSR/`build:ssr` setup — out of scope for a behaviour-preserving hop.
Restored the trailing newline on package.json that the ng update rewrite dropped.

package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified by deleting node_modules and running a plain `npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps needed), then `npm run build`, `npm run build:ssr` and the test command.
manual_followups: `npm run test` still fails exactly as at baseline: angular.json's test target lists "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so webpack reports a load error and karma aborts before any spec runs. Left untouched to keep this hop to the upgrade; it keeps hiding real test breakage in every later hop and is worth fixing on its own.

`BrowserModule.withServerTransition({ appId: 'ng-cli-universal' })` is deprecated in Angular 18 (the app id now comes from the `APP_ID` token). It still works in v18 but is likely to be removed in a later major, so a person should move to plain `BrowserModule` plus `{ provide: APP_ID, useValue: 'ng-cli-universal' }`.

`HTTP_INTERCEPTORS` is still imported in src/app/app.module.ts but unused (it was already unused before this hop, and providers only registers provideHttpClient). Safe to delete; left alone to keep the diff to the migration.
rxjs is still 6.6.7. Angular 18 and @ngrx 18 both still accept it, but rxjs 6 is end-of-life and Angular 19 drops it from the peer range, so the move to rxjs 7 must happen in the next hop.

The optional `use-application-builder` migration is still pending. Angular 19 keeps the webpack `browser` builder but marks it legacy, so adopting the esbuild `application` builder (together with rethinking the `build:ssr` target) is the main piece of deferred work on the build side.

The SSR entry still looks like dead code: Startup.cs uses UseSpa/UseAngularCliServer and never UseSpaPrerendering, and aspnet-prerendering is a 2018-era package. Consider removing the server target and aspnet-prerendering entirely.
add-employee.component.ts still uses the Untyped* form classes from the v14 opt-out; adopting typed reactive forms is still open.
`useDefineForClassFields: false` is still set in tsconfig.json from the v15 migration; a person should decide whether the app can move to the standard `true` behaviour.

`npm run lint` is still broken from the v13 hop: the tslint architect targets were deleted and nothing replaced them. The project should move to @angular-eslint and drop tslint/codelyzer from optionalDependencies.
angular.json still carries `defaultConfiguration: ""` on the build and server targets from the v12 migration.
node-sass 4.x still fails to build its native binding on modern Node and is skipped as an optional dependency; it is unused by the build but should be dropped or replaced with `sass`.
core-js is still pinned at ^2.6.5 and @types/node at ^12, both far behind the Node 20 toolchain this hop runs on.
The app still uses NgModules rather than standalone components, and the old `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` directives rather than the built-in control flow. Not adopted on purpose; Angular 18 supports both.
`npm install` still reports 94 vulnerabilities, almost all from the stale optionalDependencies (protractor, tslint, node-sass, ts-node 5) rather than from Angular itself.
